papers.what_it_is: A proof-of-concept variational hybrid CV-DV algorithm, run mostly by classical emulation on 1D models and partly on superconducting oscillator-transmon hardware, that evolves a superposition of frozen Gaussians for adiabatic nuclear dynamics.

assertions.value: The authors describe a proof-of-concept variational hybrid CV-DV algorithm for simulating adiabatic nuclear dynamics that uses qubit rotation gates and conditional displacement (CD) gates to embed a superposition of squeezed states/frozen Gaussians (FGs) onto the register.
quotes: This work presents a proof-of-concept variational hybrid CV-DV algorithm for simulating adiabatic nuclear dynamics.
The VQA uses qubit rotation gates and conditional displacement (CD) gates to embed a superposition of squeezed states/frozen Gaussians (FGs) representing the nuclear wave function onto the register.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of Gaussians embedded in the register is controlled by the number of ancilla qubits and that, consequently, the number of Gaussians scales exponentially with the allotted computational resources.
quotes: The number of Gaussians embedded in the register is controlled by the number of ancilla qubits.
Consequently, the number of Gaussians scales exponentially with the allotted computational resources.
